audit.whatIsWrong: Five separate strings claim Mel's W Rebuttal reflects Flamespitter back at Rumble ('reflect your Flamespitter empowered damage back through the cone', 'reflect the sustained magic damage back onto you', 'she can reflect the empowered damage back through it').
audit.why: Rebuttal 'reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker, prevents her from taking damage'. Flamespitter is a 3-second frontal cone with no projectile flag in Rumble's kit — it is negated by the damage immunity, not returned. The abilities that CAN be reflected are Rumble's projectile-flagged ones: Electro Harpoon (E) and The Equalizer (R). This inverts the lane plan: walking into a live Rebuttal costs a wasted Danger Zone window, it does not kill you.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal eats a committed Flamespitter outright (damage immunity); only the projectile follow-up — Electro Harpoon — is what actually bounces back.
sources: champ-data/_kits/rumble.json (Q Flamespitter has no projectile flag; E and R do)

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] and 'late' call Mel's R a reflect ('hold your Scrap Shield for her R reflect attempt', 'Watch for her R reflect'). Golden Eclipse is not a reflect.
audit.why: Golden Eclipse is a global execute (range 25000) that 'strikes all enemies marked with Overwhelm regardless of their distance from her'. Conflating it with Rebuttal teaches the wrong dodge: there is no positional counterplay to a global, so the real rule is to leave lane above her execute threshold rather than to hold a defensive cooldown for it.
audit.corrected: Golden Eclipse is global — distance is irrelevant. Manage the Overwhelm stack count and your HP before you disengage, not your Scrap Shield timing.

audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[0].why and breakdown.early both open with the boilerplate 'Flamespitter wins every melee level 1 — walk at them.' Mel is a ranged champion.
audit.why: Mel's Q Radiant Volley has 950 range against Flamespitter's 600. There is no walk-up level-1 trade to win; telling a Rumble player to walk at her feeds free Overwhelm stacks into the exact resource that powers her ultimate.
audit.corrected: Mel outranges Flamespitter at level 1 — farm the edge of the cone, do not initiate.

audit.whatIsWrong: The text repeatedly tells the player to 'learn its cooldown clock' for Rebuttal but never states the number.
audit.why: Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26s. At rank 1 that is roughly a full wave cycle of complete immunity to her only defensive tool — the single most actionable number in the matchup, and vague advice to 'track it' is what the entry currently offers instead.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal is 38s at rank 1; once baited you own the lane until it returns.

audit.why: Spike framing (level 3 double-harpoon, level 6, Blackfire Torch, two items) matches the kit: Electro Harpoon carries 2 charges, and the 58.52% win rate over 622 games supports Rumble owning the two-item window.
sources: champ-data/_kits/rumble.json (E: 'Rumble can carry 2 harpoons at a time')

edits.before: At level one you and Mel are in a genuine poke standoff — her Q volleys outrange your Flamespitter and you cannot reliably get into the Danger Zone trade window without eating Overwhelm stacks first. Farm at the edge of your Q cone and accept some chip; the goal is not to win this level but to not give her a free stack lead. At level two she picks up W Rebuttal, which is your first real obstacle: if you commit your Flamespitter channel she can reflect the empowered damage back through it. Bait Rebuttal with a short E harpoon cast first — once that reflect is on its long cooldown you can step in and run your full Danger Zone Q pattern safely. By level three with both harpoon casts available you can chain E-into-E to lock her in place for the full Flamespitter duration, and she has no mobility to escape it; this is your first genuine kill window if she is already partially chipped.

edits.before: At two-plus items you are the carry in this pairing — your Equalizer becomes a teamfight win condition that does not require you to stand in range of her volleys, and your Danger Zone sustained damage at full build outlasts her execute math in prolonged skirmishes. Play teamfights by landing Equalizer on the entry point, then walking into the wall yourself to chain the Danger Zone window; she will have to choose between staying in the Equalizer burn or stepping out and losing the angle. Watch for her R reflect in the mid-game window around first item — a well-timed reflect on an Equalizer could be devastating — but at two items your burst through Shadowflame or Luden's means no single reflect swings the result of a full team engagement.

Her reflect is W Rebuttal, not her ultimate, and it only returns projectiles — it eats a Flamespitter cone rather than bouncing it, so walking into a live Rebuttal costs you a wasted Danger Zone window rather than a reversed one.

notes: The packet flagged wants.you[2] 'Use Equalizer' as a probable wrong ability name. FALSE POSITIVE — that is ordinary shorthand for The Equalizer, not a misnamed ability; no edit proposed. Separately, the whole 'full' layer for this matchup refers to Mel with male pronouns ('his Solar Snare', 'if he gets ahead') in winCon, breakdown.mid, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.late and report[]. I fixed only tldr; the rest is templated boilerplate and would need a pass over the generator rather than nine hand edits. Also note for the kit library: rumble.json derives a 'terrain' flag on both W Scrap Shield and R The Equalizer, and a 'knockup' flag on W. All three are false positives from the Data Dragon wording ('pulls up a shield', 'wall of flames') — Scrap Shield is a shield plus a movement-speed burst with no displacement, and The Equalizer is a damage-and-slow zone that does not block movement. I avoided relying on those flags anywhere.
